paras: This assumes the premise that Democrats take the House; it is not a forecast. Everything below is an allegation or an open question, and each person named has not been charged unless the row says so.

Furthest along (public record): the Boasberg contempt inquiry (Noem, Blanche, Bove, Mazzara; Maximalists) and the Hennepin County review of federal agents (Bovino and agents; Populist-Nationalist Right). The second matters most because a state prosecution is outside a presidential pardon.

Reported, with an oversight body already looking: Guilfoyle (Primacist Hawks), Kushner and Lutnick (Deal-Capital Network), Sacks and the DOGE staff (Tech-Right), Feinberg and Hegseth (Pentagon Network).
Anonymous-source whispers: the DOJ probe of DHS contracts under Noem and Lewandowski, and the Homan sting. Neither is confirmed on the record; both have denials.

Money-for-favors theories (Operation, Deal-Capital Network, Tech-Right, Vance Lane): these need a proven link between a payment and an official act. The reporting shows timing and amounts, not that link.

Pardon limit: a pardon can cover federal crimes, but not state charges, civil suits, congressional subpoenas, or inspector general reports. Trump could also pardon himself or allies before leaving office; whether that holds up in court is untested.

What changes with a Democratic House: subpoena power, public hearings and criminal referrals. Charges would still need a Justice Department or state prosecutor willing to bring them, and statutes of limitations (generally five years for federal crimes) set the clock.
Added Oct 29: the CFTC oil-trade review (anonymous sources), the CREW suit over Kushner's envoy role (Oct 14) and Guilfoyle's Oct 13 resignation.

Sources for the legal exposure tables: Boasberg and D.C. Circuit contempt coverage; CNN, CBS and WaPo on the Lewandowski probe; WSJ and AP on Guilfoyle; ABC on the Homan sting; Axios on the Democracy Defenders Fund complaint; GAO and Swalwell filings on Pulte; Al Jazeera, NYT and DOJ lobbying filings on Srpska; WSJ and The Block on World Liberty and Binance; CREW filings on Kushner and the Qatari jet; NYT on Sacks; ABC on DOGE and the Hatch Act; Public Citizen and Mediaite on ballroom donors; Yahoo on the Hennepin review; Bloomberg Government on Oversight’s plans; Warren and Judiciary Democrats’ letters. A claim is only as strong as its tier in each row.
title: Legal exposure across factions
